open_questions.text: Should the supplier provide templates for the College's twelve most used forms, and how are these templates specified?
What is the expected data volume for migrating the signed records held in the current tool by 2027-02-28?
Is the optional on-premises deployment option required to be priced separately, and what are the infrastructure prerequisites?
What support channels and escalation paths are expected for responding to severity-one incidents within one hour at any time of day?
Does the College's existing REST API support webhook subscriptions, or must the service poll for record updates?
What data format and schema are used by the current tool for storing signed records that need to be migrated by 2027-02-28?

approach.text: Bid compliance: assemble the proposal as a single PDF of at most 20 pages and submit it through the College's procurement portal by 2026-12-01 12:00 UTC, and ensure the service is live for students by 2027-01-11, the first day of spring enrollment, integrating with the College's student records system through its existing REST API.
approach.basis: The instructions specify the format, page limit, deadline, go-live date, and API integration requirement. The order of submission is an assumption to ensure compliance.

approach.text: Audit and document management: keep an audit record of every signature event, including the signer's identity, the time, and the document version, and store signed documents for ten years.
approach.basis: The audit record details and the ten-year storage duration are explicitly stated. The underlying storage medium is an assumption.

approach.text: Signing accessibility and notifications: support signing on current desktop and mobile browsers, and send a reminder to each signer who has not signed within 72 hours.
approach.basis: Browser compatibility and the 72-hour reminder timeframe are explicitly stated. The reminder delivery channel is an assumption.

approach.text: Service availability: maintain service availability of 99.5% of the time in each calendar month, excluding planned maintenance announced five working days in advance.
approach.basis: The availability percentage and planned maintenance notice period are explicitly stated.

risks.condition: The proposal must be submitted as a single PDF of no more than 20 pages by 2026-12-01 12:00 UTC under REQ-0009.
risks.event: The final document exceeds 20 pages during last-minute edits, or portal congestion delays the 2026-12-01 12:00 UTC upload.
risks.effect: The proposal is disqualified instantly without review, losing the bid entirely.
assumptions: The team can finalize content well within the 20-page limit without last-minute overflow.
risks.trigger: The draft reaches 18 pages one week before submission, or the portal is untested.
responses: Perform a dry-run upload via the procurement portal one week before the deadline.
risks.residual_exposure: A technical outage of the procurement portal in the final hour before the deadline.

risks.condition: The service must go live for students by 2027-01-11, leaving only 41 days from the submission deadline of 2026-12-01 to build, test, and integrate.
risks.event: Integration complexities with the College's student records system REST API delay the go-live past 2027-01-11.
risks.effect: The service fails to launch on the first day of spring enrollment, disrupting student registration.
assumptions: The College's existing REST API is fully documented and immediately accessible for testing.
risks.trigger: API sandbox credentials are not provided within three days of contract award.
responses: Request API documentation and sandbox access prior to contract award.
Build a mock API server to enable parallel frontend and backend integration testing.
risks.residual_exposure: Undocumented rate limits or unexpected authentication quirks in the College's live REST API.

risks.condition: Migration of signed records held in the current tool is scheduled as a should requirement (REQ-0017) by 2027-02-28, while ten-year document storage (REQ-0016) is mandatory.
risks.event: Resources are pulled away from migration to handle spring enrollment support, causing migration to slip past 2027-02-28.
risks.effect: Historical signed records remain trapped in the legacy tool, complicating audits and ten-year retention compliance.
assumptions: Legacy data export formats are compatible with the new ingestion pipeline.
risks.trigger: Migration script development is delayed past 2027-01-15 due to enrollment support priorities.
responses: Allocate dedicated data engineering resources separate from the core go-live delivery team.
Define a prioritized batch migration schedule starting with the most recent records.
risks.residual_exposure: Incomplete legacy records requiring manual data cleanup and exception handling.
